 REPORT: LaNorris Sellers a game-time decision against Arkansas
 ESPN's Pete Thamel provided the latest update on LaNorris Sellers' status for Saturday's matchup against Arkansas.
 Alex Jones 84 
 South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers will be a game-time decision for the matchup against Arkansas , according to a report from ESPN's Pete Thamel on Saturday morning.
 Sellers injured his ankle late in the first half in the win over Texas A&M last week. The Gamecocks' signal caller returned in the second half and led the team to victory with a 41-yard touchdown run. Sellers has been listed as probable since Thursday SEC Student-Athlete Availability Report.
 Here's the full report on Sellers from Thamel on Saturday morning.
 "Sources: LaNorris Sellers' status is in flux today for South Carolina. He made the trip to Arkansas and is expected to be available, and it'll be a decision at game-time whether he goes or Cutter Woods gets his first career start. Sellers has been listed as probable as he deals with a lower body injury."
 This season, Sellers has completed 172-of-274 passes for 2,100 yards, 17 touchdowns and seven interceptions while rushing for a team high 637 yards and seven scores on 104 carries.
 Woods, who's in his second year in the program, has completed 11-of-17 passes for 100 yards, one touchdown and one interception in five games played this season.
 South Carolina and Arkansas will face off for the first time since 2022 when the Razorbacks defeated the Gamecocks, 44-30, in Fayetteville. The last win for the Gamecocks in Fayetteville came in 2013, a 52-7 victory. In the overall series, the Razorbacks own a 14-10 advantage.
 Kickoff between South Carolina and Arkansas on Saturday is set for 7:45 p.m. and will be televised on SEC Network.
